bibliographic.title: YouZhi: Towards High-Concurrency Financial LLMs via Adaptive GQA-to-MLA Transition
bibliographic.authors: Postal Savings Bank of China & Huawei LLM Team
bibliographic.citation_apa: Postal Savings Bank of China & Huawei LLM Team. (2024). YouZhi: Towards High-Concurrency Financial LLMs via Adaptive GQA-to-MLA Transition [Preprint].

methodology.method_family: model architecture adaptation, knowledge distillation, supervised fine-tuning, benchmark and deployment evaluation
methodology.study_design: experimental technical evaluation with architectural transition pipeline and comparative benchmarking
methodology.sample_description: Financial benchmark tasks; proprietary financial data for finetuning; high-concurrency mobile banking application scenario
methodology.technology_context: YouZhi-LLM with layer-adaptive GQA-to-MLA transition, KV-cache compression, Huawei Ascend ecosystem, vLLM-Ascend deployment, financial domain post-training

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The paper primarily addresses architectural efficiency and high-concurrency deployment of financial LLMs, not conversational governance, accountability, human oversight, auditability, or compliance governance mechanisms.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the study concerns financial LLMs and mentions mobile banking interaction and safety-compliant response generation, its central contribution is KV-cache optimization via GQA-to-MLA transition, training pipeline efficiency, and benchmark/deployment performance. It does not frame, evaluate, or propose governance of conversational AI systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: The provided full-text excerpts clearly center on model efficiency and deployment metrics rather than governance topics in scope.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal reflects technical research quality only. The study is methodologically coherent for efficiency-focused financial LLM engineering, but offers little transparent detail on proprietary datasets and does not discuss governance, ethics, or oversight.

cerqual.explanation: Confidence in using this study as evidence for conversational governance in regulated LLM systems is low because the text supports technical performance and deployment claims, not governance mechanisms, oversight, accountability, or compliance processes.

coding.theme: Efficient deployment of domain-specific financial LLMs
coding.subtheme: Architectural compression and concurrency scaling for banking inference

synthesis.main_claim: YouZhi-LLM improves financial LLM deployment efficiency and benchmark performance through layer-adaptive GQA-to-MLA transition, domain post-training, and Ascend-native inference, yielding higher concurrency with limited accuracy loss.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes an adaptive structural transition framework and training pipeline to reduce KV-cache overhead and increase maximum concurrency for financial LLM inference while improving financial benchmark scores.
synthesis.limitations: Evaluation relies on proprietary financial finetuning data; broader governance, safety governance design, and conversational control mechanisms are not developed; ecosystem dependence on Huawei Ascend may limit transferability.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting governance evidence. May serve only as peripheral contextual background on financial LLM deployment constraints in banking if the review separately covers operational scalability.

evidence.claim: Paper focuses on LLM deployment efficiency for financial applications, not conversational governance.
evidence.excerpt: their high-concurrency deployment is severely bottlenecked by KV cache memory overhead

evidence.claim: Core contribution is architectural GQA-to-MLA transition for financial LLMs.
evidence.excerpt: YouZhi-LLM features a layer-adaptive GQA-to-MLA transition framework that dynamically assigns per-layer FreqFold sizes

evidence.claim: Study is situated in regulated high-stakes financial services.
evidence.excerpt: Real-world financial services, as exemplified by high-concurrency mobile banking scenarios

evidence.claim: Mobile banking scenario includes conversational interaction demands but governance is not the research focus.
evidence.excerpt: core interaction demandsprecise intent recognition, strict slot filling, and safety-compliant response generation

evidence.claim: Reported outcomes emphasize benchmark accuracy and concurrency gains.
evidence.excerpt: YouZhi-7B yields a 12.3% improvement in average financial benchmark score alongside a 2.69× increase in maximum concurrency

evidence.claim: Training combines distillation and financial supervised fine-tuning on proprietary data.
evidence.excerpt: integrates generalized knowledge distillation with financial-specific supervised fine-tuning

evidence.claim: Deployment evaluation uses Ascend NPUs and vLLM-Ascend.
evidence.excerpt: when evaluated on Ascend NPUs via vLLM-Ascend, the massive KV-cache reduction translates directly into deployment efficiency

evidence.claim: Conclusion reiterates efficiency-oriented financial LLM contribution.
evidence.excerpt: we present YouZhi-LLM, an efficient financial large language model natively built on the Huawei Ascend ecosystem
